t: Everything to install Mira, connect it to your Jellyfin, watch at home and away, and with friends. Mira is a free Jellyfin client for Windows, Mac and iPhone. Jellyfin keeps your films and series on a computer of yours and serves them; Mira is the pleasant way to watch them. No Mira account, no ads, and nothing leaves your server.

Device · What it needs · Guide Windows · Windows 10 (2004 or later) or 11, x64 · Install on Windows Mac · Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 15 or later · Install on Mac iPhone and iPad · iOS 26 or later, AltStore Classic, a free Apple ID · Install on iPhone There is no Mira for Android for now. Mira web, which Jellyfin used to serve to phones in the browser, ended with 0.9.4.

A Jellyfin server, 10.9 or later, on a computer that stays on, and an account on it. No server yet? Mira for Windows installs Jellyfin and sets it up for you: see Set up Jellyfin. Your films and series in Jellyfin's folders, named the way it recognises them. To watch away from home: Tailscale, free. Mira has it built in, so most devices need nothing more. See Away from home.

On the computer that will hold your videos, install Mira for Windows and choose No server yet: Mira installs Jellyfin on this PC. Put your videos in the Movies, Shows and Anime folders it creates. Open the guide (F1) and click Set everything up on the Mira on your iPhone card. Install Mira on your other devices and sign in with the same account. Send your party link to a friend and watch together.

Search this wiki with the field at the top of the page, or press /. Troubleshooting lists the messages Mira shows and what to do. Ask on Discord, or report a bug on GitHub. Note Mira is a preview: it is used every day, but some things have not been tried on every setup yet (HDR, multichannel audio, several monitors). Mira is an independent project, not affiliated with Jellyfin, and provides no films.

Download Mira for Windows, get past SmartScreen, add the video engine and keep Mira up to date. Download The latest release has three files for Windows. One is enough. File · For Installer · Most people. Installs Mira for your Windows account only, without administrator rights, with a Start menu shortcut. Portable · One file that runs as it is. Keep it in a folder of its own, like Documents\Mira: it creates its data folder next to itself. Zip · The whole application folder. Extract the entire Mira folder somewhere you can write, never just Mira.exe. The .NET runtime is included: there is nothing else to install.

Mira's Windows files are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Click More info, then Run anyway. You can check first that your file is the published one: each file has a .sha256 next to it in the release. Get-FileHash .\Mira-__VERSION__-win-x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 The value must match the one in the .sha256 file.

Open Mira. The first time, a welcome screen explains what Jellyfin and Mira each do. Mira looks for Jellyfin on this PC, on your home network and on your Tailscale devices, and fills in the address it finds. Enter your Jellyfin username and password, then Sign in. More in Sign in to Jellyfin. No Jellyfin yet? Choose No server yet: Mira installs Jellyfin on this PC. See Set up Jellyfin.

Mira plays with mpv. Its engine (31 MB) is not inside Mira's files: Mira downloads a precise build from mpv's Windows builds on SourceForge and checks its SHA-256 before using it. With the installer, leave Download the mpv video engine ticked. Otherwise, Mira offers it at the first playback, or in Settings → Playback → Install the mpv engine. Already have mpv.net or Jellyfin MPV Shim? Mira reuses their engine and downloads nothing. You can also pick another 64-bit libmpv-2.dll in Settings → Playback.

Mira updates itself. A few seconds after it opens, then every 6 hours, it asks GitHub for a new version, downloads it in the background, checks that it is signed by Mira with the announced size and SHA-256, and installs it when you close Mira. Restart in the notice installs it right away. To stop the automatic check, turn off Settings → Mira on this PC → Update automatically. The Search button stays. Your settings and session live in the data folder and are never touched by an update.

Settings → Apps → Mira. The uninstaller asks before deleting your data (no by default), then lists what remains on the PC: Jellyfin if Mira installed it, the "Mira - Jellyfin" firewall rule, and Jellyfin's read access to your video folders.

Install Mira on a Mac with the disk image or Homebrew, allow it the first time, and let it update itself. Mira for Mac plays your Jellyfin library with the same mpv player as on Windows. It needs a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 15 Sequoia or later, and a Jellyfin server you already have: Mira for Mac does not install Jellyfin.
Download Mira-__VERSION__-mac-arm64.dmg. Open it and drag Mira onto Applications. Open Mira from Applications. macOS stops it the first time: see below.

If you use Homebrew, one command in Terminal replaces steps 1 and 2: brew install --cask sasou-web/mira/mira It comes from Mira's own tap, sasou-web/homebrew-mira: Homebrew's main catalogue only takes apps notarised by Apple. Homebrew checks the image's SHA-256 and keeps macOS's protection, so the first opening is the same as below. Mira then updates itself; brew uninstall --cask --zap mira removes it with its settings.

Mira is not signed with a paid Apple developer account, so macOS cannot check it and refuses to open it the first time. Once only: Open Mira, then close the message. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security. At the bottom, next to "Mira was blocked", click Open Anyway, then confirm. If macOS says Mira is "damaged", or the button does not appear, type this in Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Mira.app It only removes the "downloaded from the Internet" mark from Mira. It changes no security setting of your Mac.

Type your server's address (192.168.1.20, nas:8096…), your username and password. Mira finds the right port and protocol. Away from home, use the server's Tailscale address, or let Built-in Tailscale reach it without the Tailscale app. Your password is never stored: Mira keeps only the session Jellyfin opens, in your Mac's keychain (item "Mira"). The rest is in ~/Library/Application Support/Mira, readable by your macOS account only.

Mira updates itself. When it opens, then every 6 hours, it asks GitHub for a new version, downloads the disk image and keeps it only if its size and SHA-256 match the release's signed manifest. It installs it when you quit Mira, or right away with Restart in the notice. Note When Mira updates itself, the old version hands your session over to the new one as it quits, so macOS does not ask for anything (from the version after 0.9.4: the update to it still asks once). After an update made another way (Homebrew, or the disk image dragged by hand), macOS asks once for your login password so that Mira can read its own keychain item: choose Always Allow. This happens because Mira is not signed by an Apple developer account. If you refuse, Mira simply asks you to sign in to Jellyfin again. Mira cannot replace itself when it runs from the disk image, from the Downloads folder (macOS runs a protected copy), or from a folder your account cannot change. It still downloads and checks the new version, and Open the disk image lets you drag it to Applications. To stop the automatic check, turn off Settings → Mira on this Mac → Update automatically.

Mira follows your trackpad settings (natural scrolling, swipe between pages). In the library: swipe with two fingers to go back and forward (the page follows your fingers, as in Safari; let go early to stay), pinch to change the size of the posters, force click a poster for its menu. In the player: swipe left or right to seek, up or down for the volume; spread two fingers for full screen, pinch to leave it, then to shrink the player to the mini player.
Sign out first (Settings → Account & server), quit Mira, then delete ~/Library/Application Support/Mira.

Mira for iPhone is a native app installed with AltStore Classic and a free Apple ID, refreshed each week by a PC at home. Mira for iPhone and iPad is a real app, with your library, search, its own player (Picture in Picture, AirPlay, next episode), the sleep timer, Watch together and, away from home, Built-in Tailscale. It is not on the App Store: you install it with AltStore Classic, free, which signs it on your iPhone with your own Apple ID.

iOS 26 or later (iPhone 11 and later). A free Apple ID is enough. Apple then signs at most 3 apps at a time (AltStore counts as one), and each app expires after 7 days unless it is refreshed. AltStore refreshes it in the background when your iPhone is on the same Wi-Fi as a PC running AltServer: the PC that runs Jellyfin, always on, is perfect for this. AltServer runs on Windows (and macOS). The steps below are for Windows. Privacy You type your Apple ID and password in AltServer, which sends them to Apple only, to create the free certificate. AltStore downloads Mira's source from miracinema.app and the app from GitHub. Mira itself talks only to your Jellyfin, and to Tailscale only if you turn Built-in Tailscale on.

On the PC that runs Jellyfin, with your usual Windows account: Install iTunes and iCloud from Apple's website, not from the Microsoft Store (AltServer cannot find the Store versions): iTunes 64-bit iCloud Uninstall any Microsoft Store version first. Don't sign in to iCloud: this version refuses anyway ("Update iCloud for Windows"), click OK then Cancel, and don't update it. Download AltServer for Windows, unzip it and run Setup.exe. Search for AltServer in Windows, right-click → Run as administrator. If the firewall asks, allow private networks only. A diamond icon appears near the clock. If its menu offers Launch at Login, tick it. Refreshing only works while a Windows session is open on the PC with AltServer running.

Plug the iPhone into the PC, unlock it and tap Trust. Open iTunes, sign in with your Apple ID, click the iPhone icon, then in Summary tick Sync with this iPhone over Wi-Fi and click Apply. This is what allows refreshing without a cable. AltServer icon → Install AltStore → your iPhone. Enter your Apple ID and password. Wait for AltServer's notification. If AltStore's icon does not appear, restart the iPhone. On the iPhone: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, tap your Apple ID, then Trust. Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode: turn it on. The iPhone restarts and asks you to confirm. Settings → General → Background App Refresh: leave it on for AltStore.

Open AltStore → Sources → +, and add: https://miracinema.app/altstore.json Open the Mira source → Mira → FREE. AltStore downloads the app, signs it and installs it. Open Mira and sign in to Jellyfin. The first time on your home Wi-Fi, iOS asks for access to the local network: tap Allow, or Mira cannot see Jellyfin at home. You can also sign in with a code: Sign in with a code shows six digits, which an administrator approves in Mira for Windows or Mac (Settings → Friends & guests → Allow a device) or in Jellyfin's web page. Quick Connect must be turned on in Jellyfin.

Updates: AltStore shows each new version of Mira in My Apps; tap Update. Expiry: My Apps shows the days left. As long as the PC is on with AltServer and the iPhone visits its Wi-Fi once a week, AltStore refreshes by itself. Otherwise, open AltStore at home and tap Refresh All. An expired app no longer opens but loses nothing. Away from home: see Away from home.

"Could not find AltServer" while refreshing: the iPhone and the PC are not on the same Wi-Fi, AltServer is not running, or iTunes' Wi-Fi sync is off. AltStore installed from Safari: that is AltStore PAL (European Union), which only installs apps notarised by Apple, so not Mira. Delete it and install AltStore Classic with AltServer. AltServer doesn't see the iPhone: check that iTunes and iCloud come from Apple's website, then unplug and plug the unlocked iPhone again. AltStore's own guides: install on Windows, troubleshooting.

Let Mira install Jellyfin on a Windows PC, name your videos so Jellyfin recognises them, and get the server ready for your other devices. Jellyfin is the server: it keeps your films and series, their artwork and everyone's progress. Mira is the player. Jellyfin runs on one computer that stays on; Mira runs on every device you watch on. Already have Jellyfin 10.9 or later? Skip to Get the server ready.

On the Windows PC that will keep your videos, in Mira's sign-in screen, choose No server yet: Mira installs Jellyfin on this PC, then: Videos folder: Videos\Jellyfin by default, or another one with Browse (a storage drive, for example). Mira creates Movies, Shows and Anime in it. Username and password: they become Jellyfin's administrator account. Install. Mira downloads Jellyfin's official installer from repo.jellyfin.org, checks its SHA-256 against the one Jellyfin publishes, and runs it. Windows asks for permission once: Jellyfin installs for the whole PC, as a service that starts with Windows. Mira then fills in Jellyfin's first-run wizard: your administrator account, three libraries (Movies, Shows, Anime), access from the Internet turned off. Then it signs you in. Tip If Jellyfin's installer shows "Could not start the Jellyfin Server service", choose Ignore. The service usually starts right after, and Mira carries on as soon as Jellyfin answers. Jellyfin's service runs as Windows' Network Service account, which cannot read your personal folders. Mira gives it read-only access to Movies, Shows and Anime, and nothing else in the folder you chose.

Jellyfin finds the title, poster and summary of each video from its folder and file name. Put one folder per film, one folder per series with a folder per season: Movies\Spirited Away (2001)\Spirited Away (2001).mkv Shows\Arcane\Season 01\Arcane - S01E03.mkv Anime\Frieren\Season 01\Frieren - S01E01.mkv The year in brackets avoids mix-ups between films of the same name. Subtitle files next to a video, with the same name and a language (Spirited Away (2001).en.srt), are found too. New files appear after Jellyfin's next scan. Refresh in Mira's library asks Jellyfin to scan right away (administrator account). Note Copy or move videos into these folders with File Explorer: they take the folder's access rights. A file moved by another program can keep the rights of its old folder and stay invisible to Jellyfin; copy it with File Explorer instead.

On the PC that runs Jellyfin, signed in with Jellyfin's administrator account, open the guide (? on the left, or F1). The Mira on your iPhone card ticks what is ready and numbers what is left: Mira's extension on Jellyfin: it serves your party link, guests without an account, automatic subtitles and a few other features. Windows Firewall: lets your devices reach Jellyfin, on its port only, from your home network and Tailscale, never on a public network. If Windows counts your home Wi-Fi as public, Make it private changes it (only at home: a café's network must stay public). Away from home (optional): Tailscale on this PC. From power-on: Jellyfin starts with Windows, before anyone signs in, and restarts after an error. Set everything up does all that Mira can, with a single Windows permission, then gives the address to type on your other devices. Close Jellyfin to the network, under the steps, removes Mira's firewall rule; Set everything up puts it back.

To add Mira's extension from Jellyfin's web page: Dashboard → Plugins → Repositories → +, name Mira, URL: https://github.com/sasou-web/Mira/releases/latest/download/jellyfin-manifest.json Catalog → Mira → Install, then restart Jellyfin (Dashboard → Restart). Jellyfin then updates the extension with each version of Mira. With a Windows PC, prefer Set everything up: Mira checks the extension's signature before installing it.

In Mira for Windows, on the Jellyfin PC: Settings → Maintenance → Jellyfin on this PC shows its version and last backup (Jellyfin 10.11 or later). Back up now makes Jellyfin's built-in backup: accounts, everyone's progress, libraries, artwork and settings, not your videos. Mira can copy each backup to another drive and keeps the three most recent there. It reminds you after 30 days without one. When a newer Jellyfin comes out, Mira says so once. Update Jellyfin backs up first, downloads the official installer, checks it, then Windows asks for permission. It is refused while someone is watching. Careful A backup holds the sign-in tokens of your devices. Keep it in a folder of your own, never a shared one. To restore one: install Jellyfin (same version or later), copy jellyfin-backup-<date>.zip into C:\ProgramData\Jellyfin\Server\data\backups, open http://127.0.0.1:8096 → Dashboard → Backups, and restore it.

Which address to type, how Mira finds your server, and why it sometimes asks before sending your password. Mira looks for your server As long as no address is known, the sign-in screen looks for Jellyfin for a couple of seconds: on this computer, on your home network (Jellyfin's own discovery), and on your devices that are online on Tailscale. It fills in the best address it finds and says where it found it; the other servers are offered next to it. Search again looks once more. An address you typed is never replaced. The iPhone cannot discover servers on the home network (Apple only allows it to paid developer accounts): type the address, or use Tailscale.

Mira accepts the address in almost any form: You type · Mira tries 192.168.1.20 · the PC at home, port 8096 nas:8096 · a name on your network, with its port 100.101.102.103 or jellyfin-pc · the PC's address or name on Tailscale https://jellyfin.example.com · a server on the Internet an address copied from Jellyfin's web page · the same server Without http:// or https://, Mira tries HTTPS, then port 8096, then HTTP, and shows the address it kept. Tip On the Jellyfin PC itself, the address is http://127.0.0.1:8096. For your other devices, the guide's Mira on your iPhone card gives the right one. A Tailscale address works at home as well as away.

s: When Mira asks before signing in
t: Mira checks the address before your password leaves: "This isn't a Jellyfin server": something answers, but not Jellyfin (a router, a NAS page, Emby). Check the port, 8096 by default. "Mira needs Jellyfin 10.9": update Jellyfin. "HTTPS certificate not recognised": Mira never falls back to http:// by itself, since your password would travel in clear. For a server at home, type its full http:// address. "This address goes over the Internet, in http://": your password would cross the Internet unencrypted. Use the server's https:// address or its Tailscale address. Sign in anyway sends it regardless. At home, on this PC and over Tailscale, nothing is asked: Tailscale already encrypts everything.

Mira for iPhone can sign in without typing a password: Sign in with a code shows six digits. An administrator approves them in Mira for Windows or Mac (Settings → Friends & guests → Allow a device), choosing the account, or in Jellyfin's web page. Jellyfin's Quick Connect must be on (Dashboard → General).

Your password is never stored. Mira keeps only the session Jellyfin opens: protected by Windows for your account, in the keychain on Mac and iPhone. Sign out closes the session on Jellyfin too. On Windows and Mac, Also erase this account's data on this PC removes the cache and artwork of that account.

Your preferred languages, Skip intros and recaps, the audio and subtitles chosen for each series and the titles removed from Continue watching are kept on your Jellyfin account, and follow you to your other devices. The most recent choice wins. Appearance and home rows stay on each device.

Reach your Jellyfin from anywhere with Tailscale, built into Mira on Windows, Mac and iPhone, without opening anything to the Internet. At home, Mira reaches Jellyfin directly. Away, it goes through Tailscale: a free private network between your own devices, encrypted end to end. Jellyfin stays closed to the rest of the Internet. Careful Don't open a port on your router to reach Jellyfin: it would expose it to the whole Internet. Tailscale does the same job without that risk.

The PC that runs Jellyfin needs the real Tailscale app, signed in to your Tailscale account. Install Tailscale from tailscale.com/download and sign in. A free personal account is enough. In Mira for Windows, open the guide (F1) and click Set everything up on the Mira on your iPhone card. It opens Jellyfin to your Tailscale devices in the firewall, turns on Tailscale's Run unattended (so it works before anyone signs in to Windows), and keeps the PC awake on mains power. The card then gives the Tailscale address to type on your devices. It works at home too. If the PC sleeps, Tailscale cannot wake it. On a laptop on mains power, set closing the lid to Do nothing.

Each device can either have the Tailscale app, or use Built-in Tailscale, which is inside Mira. Built-in Tailscale makes Mira one more device on your Tailscale network, only while Mira is open. When the Tailscale app is connected on a device, Mira uses it and does not offer its own.

On the sign-in screen, type the Jellyfin PC's Tailscale address (100.x.y.z) or its name. Mira offers Sign in to Tailscale; it also does when it finds no server. Your browser opens Tailscale's sign-in page. Sign in with the account of the Jellyfin PC. If your Tailscale network approves each new device, approve mira-<computer name> in its admin console (Open Tailscale's admin console). If the firewall asks to allow Mira's Tailscale, accept: the direct connection is faster. Refusing works too, through a Tailscale relay. Sign in to Jellyfin as usual. Mira then joins your Tailscale network each time it opens and leaves when it closes. Settings → Account & server → Built-in Tailscale shows its state and the path Mira takes: At home (direct), Through the Tailscale app or Through Built-in Tailscale.

Mira → Settings → Away from home → turn on Built-in Tailscale, then Sign in to Tailscale. Not signed in to Jellyfin yet: on the sign-in screen, Away from home: Built-in Tailscale. Tailscale's page opens over Mira: sign in with the account of the Jellyfin PC. Mira closes it once the iPhone is connected. Your Tailscale password stays on Tailscale's page. If your network approves each new device, approve mira-iphone in the admin console. From the sign-in screen, Mira finds Jellyfin on your Tailscale network. Already signed in: nothing else to do. When the Wi-Fi doesn't lead to Jellyfin, Mira goes through Built-in Tailscale. Settings → Away from home → Path to Jellyfin says which way Mira goes, and whether the Jellyfin PC is online on Tailscale. No VPN profile is needed, so it works with AltStore Classic and a free Apple ID. Through Built-in Tailscale, a video sent with AirPlay is still played by the iPhone: the TV cannot reach Jellyfin through it.

Key expiry. A Tailscale device's sign-in expires after 180 days by default. Mira warns you two weeks before. In the admin console, ⋯ → Disable key expiry on the device avoids it, for the Jellyfin PC too. Signing out. Sign out of Tailscale in Mira's settings tells Tailscale, then erases Built-in Tailscale's keys from the device. The device stays in your console, "Logged out", until you remove it there.

If Tailscale's coordination servers have an outage, devices that are already set up can keep reaching each other from the list of devices they keep. Tailscale only allows this when your network's policy says so. Mira offers it under Built-in Tailscale in its settings, with Copy the line; in your network policy, paste it just below "nodeAttrs": [ (if there is none, add the whole block after the first {): "nodeAttrs": [ { "target": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:tagged"], "attr": ["cache-network-maps"] }, ], Privacy Nothing goes to Tailscale before you sign in to it. Then, as with the Tailscale app, its servers see the account you chose, the device's name, its system and its IP addresses. Your videos stay end-to-end encrypted, directly or through a relay. Mira sends no logs to Tailscale.
To watch with someone who is not on your Tailscale network, send them your party link: it opens only Mira to the Internet, through Tailscale Funnel, never the rest of Jellyfin.

Home, films and series, search, favourites, collections, and titles kept on your computer to watch offline. Home Home opens on a large banner of your titles, then Continue watching: the films and series you started, the most recent first, one card per series, with the time left. Below come the next episodes, recently added titles and the rows you chose. Home rows (Settings → Appearance) lets you reorder rows or hide them, including a "New in…" row per library. The layout is kept per device. Right-click a card in Continue watching (long press on iPhone) and choose Remove from Continue watching to forget it until you play it again. Undo puts it back.

Movies and Shows & anime each have their own page, with genre chips, filters (genre, year, progress, library) and sorting (added, title, year, rating, last played). Favorites is a filter too. On a series' poster, a number says how many episodes are left to watch: a new episode of a series you follow shows up in the library. A title's page shows the picture of the file you would play ("4K · HDR10", "1080p") and the time it would end if you started now. On a series, it shows the next episode ("Resume · S01 E07"). Below: the cast and crew (a click shows their titles in your library), the extras (making-of, deleted scenes; trailers have their own button), similar titles and the other films of the same collection. The buttons next to Play keep their shape and only change state: Favorite, Watched, and Keep on this PC (Windows) or Keep on this Mac. Their names show on hover.

When a title has a trailer, a Trailer button shows on its page (on iPhone, in …). A trailer kept on your server plays in Mira, like a film: put it in a trailers folder next to the film, or name it Film (2020)-trailer.mkv. Otherwise, Jellyfin often knows one on YouTube (from TMDb): the button says so ("Trailer on YouTube, in your browser") and opens it in your browser, never in Mira. With Settings → Playback → Trailer before the film (Windows and Mac, off by default), a film started from the beginning plays its trailer kept on your server first, as at the cinema; Skip trailer goes straight to the film. Never a trailer from the web, never when resuming, never in a group.

A title counts as watched when it ends, when you stop past 90 %, or when you go to the next episode from the credits. You can also mark it by hand, from its page or its menu (right-click, or long press). With several seasons, Mark season as watched marks them all at once.
Ctrl + K or Ctrl + F on Windows, ⌘ + F on Mac. From two letters, Mira shows the people (actors, directors) whose name matches, then titles, episodes and collections.

On Windows and Mac, a film's or series' menu has Add to collection…: tick the collections it belongs to, or type a name to create a new one ("Friday nights", "To show Léa"). A collection can be renamed and deleted from its page; its titles stay in your library and no file moves. Home has a Collections row. You need Jellyfin's administrator account, or an account Jellyfin allows to manage collections. Tip Settings → Maintenance → Group my movies into collections (administrator) asks Jellyfin to group the films of a same saga automatically, from TMDb.

On Windows and Mac, Keep on this PC (or Keep on this Mac) on a title's page downloads the original file from Jellyfin, with its subtitles, to watch it on a train or a plane. Kept titles are in On this PC in the left rail. Mira plays them before asking Jellyfin, and the next episode follows if you kept it too. Your Jellyfin account needs the right to download.

Action · Keys Search · Ctrl + K or Ctrl + F Home, Movies, Shows, Whole library · Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 4 From a poster to its neighbour · arrow keys A poster's menu · Shift + F10, or right-click Back · Esc, Alt + ←, or the mouse's back button Getting started guide · F1

Shortcuts, intros skipped, picture in picture, sleep timer, picture and sound settings, and playback away from home. On Windows and Mac, Mira plays with mpv, in its own window: almost every file plays as it is, with its audio tracks, subtitles and chapters. On iPhone, Mira has its own player built on Apple's.

The bar shows the title and episode on the left, the chapter and time on the right. Below: play/pause, next episode and volume on the left; ⋮ (speed, sleep timer, subtitle delay, information), audio and subtitles, mini player, picture in picture and full screen on the right. Controls hide after a few seconds without moving the mouse. The seek bar is cut into chapters; hovering shows the time, the chapter and, when Jellyfin has prepared them, a preview of the picture. Volume goes up to 200 % for a title recorded too low: past 100 %, the sound is amplified then limited, without clipping. A click on the picture pauses or resumes, a double click goes full screen. A click near the bars only shows the controls, never pauses by mistake.

Action · Windows · Mac Play / pause · Space or K · Space or K Back / forward 10 seconds · ← / →, J / L · ← / →, J / L Back / forward 1 minute · Shift + ← / → · Shift + ← / → Jump to 0 %, 10 %… 90 % · 0 to 9 · 0 to 9 Volume · ↑ / ↓, mouse wheel · ↑ / ↓ Mute · M · M Subtitles off / on · C · C Full screen · F, F11, double click · F, double click Mini player · I · I, ⌘ + [ Skip the intro, recap or credits · S · S Next episode · N · N Back, leave full screen · Esc · Esc

The keyboard's play and track keys, a headset's button and the system's own controls work the player even while Mira is behind another window, the mini player and picture in picture included: Windows: the media keys, the media overlay that shows with the volume, and the play, ±10 s and next-episode buttons of Mira's taskbar thumbnail and notification-area icon. Mac: F8 (play / pause), F7 (back 10 seconds), F9 (next episode, when there is one), the button of AirPods or a headset, and Now Playing in Control Center and the menu bar, with the title, its poster, ±10 s and a bar to move through the film. In a Watch together group, they act for the group, as the player's own keys do. When the player closes, the keys go back to your other apps.

Tap to show the controls. Double tap on a side to go back or forward 10 seconds (taps add up). Swipe up or down on the left for brightness, on the right for volume, across to seek. Press and hold to play at ×2, pinch to fill the screen, swipe down to shrink the player. The lock keeps stray touches away.

s: Intros, credits and the next episode
t: Skip intro, Skip credits and recap buttons appear from Jellyfin's media segments (Jellyfin 10.10 or later, from the server or a plugin like Intro Skipper) or from the file's chapter names. With Settings → Playback → Skip intros and recaps, Mira skips them without asking, once each: going back into one plays it again. Next episode appears during the end credits or in the last 20 seconds. With Play episodes back to back, a 10-second countdown starts; Cancel stays on this episode. After 3 episodes in a row with nothing touched (keyboard, mouse, trackpad, controller, or the screen on iPhone), Mira does not start the next one: it stops at the end of the episode and asks Are you still watching?, so a night asleep in front of a series does not mark ten episodes watched. Keep watching plays the next one. Never in a watch party. To turn it off: Settings → Playback → Ask if you’re still watching. Mira resumes a little before where you stopped, 5 seconds by default, to pick up the thread (Settings → Playback). From the beginning on a title's page starts over.

s: Mini player and picture in picture
t: Mini player: the video keeps playing in a corner of the library while you browse. Drag it to any corner; on Windows, push it past the right edge to tuck it behind a tab. Picture in picture (Windows and Mac): the video in a small window of its own, above your other windows, with its subtitles. On iPhone, Apple's Picture in Picture.
In the player's ⋮ menu: pause in 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, or at the end of the episode. On iPhone, it is on the title's page. It is cleared when the player closes.

Picture (Settings → Playback, Windows and Mac): Standard (mpv's own rendering, the lightest), Cinema (the default: smooth motion on any screen, no banding in gradients) and Maximum (with the finest scaling). If the computer drops frames, Mira steps down one level by itself and tells you. Audio output (Windows and Mac, Settings → Audio & subtitles): the output device, the number of channels, and Sound sent to the amplifier as is for an amplifier or sound bar that decodes Dolby and DTS. On Windows, over HDMI, Dolby TrueHD, Atmos and DTS-HD too; on a Mac, Dolby Digital and DTS only (macOS sends nothing larger untouched), the rest decoded by Mira. Test the audio output plays a tone on each speaker. In the player, Audio switches the output, and ⋮ → Info says where the sound goes and whether it reaches the amplifier undecoded. Audio delay (⋮ menu): if lips and voices don't match, in steps of 0.1 s, until the player closes.

At home, Mira plays the file as it is. Away, a 4K film may not fit your connection: Quality (Settings → Playback and the player's ⋮ menu) sets a limit, or Auto measures the connection to Jellyfin. Under the limit, Jellyfin converts the file while you watch. If the connection drops, Mira waits for Jellyfin, reopens the stream once where it was, and only then says it cannot play. Converting is heavy for the server. On the Jellyfin PC, Mira can have the graphics card do it: Settings → Maintenance → Convert with the graphics card, tried first on one of your titles.

Your languages remembered series by series, subtitle style, files of your own, and subtitles found and synced by the server. Your languages, series by series In Settings → Audio & subtitles, list your preferred audio languages and subtitle languages, in order. Mira picks from the tracks of each file. Change the audio or subtitles of an episode, and Mira remembers it for the whole series: the next episodes get the same choice, matched by language and track name ("Full" rather than "Signs", subtitles off…). An episode without a similar track falls back on your preferred languages. These choices follow your account to your other devices. The same page sets the size and style of subtitles (dark background, white or yellow, bold, height on screen), with a preview.

The audio and subtitles menu shows both lists side by side, the current track ticked, with its language, codec and channels. Load a file… plays a subtitle file of your own (.srt, .ass, .vtt). Then Keep on Jellyfin sends it to Jellyfin, so your other devices have it too. Search for subtitles… appears when Jellyfin has a subtitle plugin, like Open Subtitles or Mira's own automatic subtitles. Mira says first what will be sent to the service. Subtitle delay (⋮ menu) shifts them if they come too early or too late, until the player closes. On iPhone, it is in the subtitles menu, in steps of 0.5 s.

Mira's extension on Jellyfin can find subtitles by itself for each new film or episode, in the languages you choose, check that they fit the video and sync them to it. On Windows and Mac, signed in as Jellyfin's administrator: Settings → Maintenance → Automatic subtitles. Choose your Languages, and whether subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing (SDH) are preferred, either, or avoided. Choose the sources: OpenSubtitles works without an account (an account only raises the daily quota); SubDL needs a free API key of yours. Test the sources, then turn on Search automatically. When a title arrives, Mira's extension looks for a match, then tries again now and then for a month if nothing is reliable enough. It never searches while something plays. It keeps a candidate only when it is sure: a file whose fingerprint matches yours, or a release from the same group and source. Before keeping it, it checks its length against the video, and Sync to the video aligns it on the file's own text track or on its speech. Log shows what was kept, set aside and why. Privacy The sources receive the file's fingerprint and size (OpenSubtitles), the title's IMDb or TMDb ids, season and episode number, title, year and language. Never the file's name, never anything about you. Everything runs on your Jellyfin server: your devices send nothing. Also search for what is already there goes through your whole library once per language. It uses your daily quota, so it can take several days.

Watch the same film at the same second as friends, each at home, with your party link, even without an account or Tailscale. Watch together keeps several devices on the same film, at the same second: when someone pauses, skips or goes to the next episode, everyone follows. It uses Jellyfin's own SyncPlay, so it works between Mira for Windows, Mac and iPhone.

For people who already have an account on your Jellyfin (your household, a friend you added): On a title's page, Watch together → Create a group and invite…. The others see the group on their Home, under the banner, and Join. Or send them the link Mira gives. Play becomes Play for the group: it starts for everyone, from your progress. Pick another title while in the group and Mira asks before replacing the group's title. While you are in a group, the player says what the group is doing ("Waiting for someone in the group…", "Paused for the group"), and an icon shows how many are in it. Leave the group when you are done.

Your party is a link, always the same, that brings a friend straight into your group, even without an account on your Jellyfin and without Tailscale. Find it in Settings → Friends & guests → Your party, and Copy it. Send it in Discord, Messages or anywhere: it shows a card with who invites and what you are watching. Your friend: Opens the link and taps Open in Mira (Mira for Windows, Mac or iPhone; the page says where to get it otherwise). Types a first name, which is what the group sees. No account to create. Is in your group, and follows along. Each guest gets a device of their own. In Guests, under your link, Take back removes one at once. Make a new link stops the old link and all its guests. If your friend has an account on your Jellyfin, the same link signs them into the group with their own account. And if the link is from another Jellyfin (a friend's party on their own server), Mira joins it as a guest, then gives you back your own account when you Leave the party.

s: How a link works from anywhere
t: The link goes through Tailscale Funnel, which opens only Mira's page and its guest gateway to the Internet, never the rest of Jellyfin: no dashboard, no sign-in page, no other route. On the Jellyfin PC, Mira for Windows opens Funnel by itself. The very first time, Tailscale asks you to allow Funnel on your account: Allow Funnel on Tailscale opens that page, once. Without Funnel, the link still works at home, and for friends on your Tailscale network. Privacy With Funnel open, the name of your Jellyfin PC on Tailscale becomes public: its HTTPS certificate is published in certificate transparency logs, like every Funnel address. Traffic stays encrypted to your PC. Each guest gets a hidden Jellyfin account that can only watch with your group, is removed when you take the guest back, and expires after 7 days without use.

Use the latest Mira on every device, and Mira's extension must be on the host's Jellyfin (see Set up Jellyfin). Each device plays from Jellyfin on its own. A friend far away needs a connection fast enough for the file, or a lower Quality in their player (see The player). Someone who loads more slowly holds the group for a moment: Mira says "Loading for the group…" rather than leaving them behind.
A map of Mira's settings on Windows, Mac and iPhone, and what each part is for. Each change applies and is saved at once: there is no Save button.

Settings open from the gear in the left rail (⌘ + , on Mac). Part · What is in it Playback · Skip intros and recaps, play episodes back to back, trailer before the film, resume where you left off, picture, quality away from home, hardware decoding, the mpv engine (Windows) Audio & subtitles · Preferred audio and subtitle languages, subtitle size and style, audio output and amplifier Appearance · Mira's language, couch mode, home rows, library density, automatic carousel, reduce animations Account & server · Your Jellyfin account and photo, sign out, Built-in Tailscale, new episode notifications, who is watching on Jellyfin right now Mira on this PC / Mac · Updates, and the titles kept to watch offline Privacy · Everything Mira sends, to whom and when, with the switch of each connection that has one Your recap · What you watched this month and this year, from Jellyfin Under Your server, for Jellyfin's administrator: Part · What is in it Friends & guests · Add a friend (an account of their own), your party link and its guests, allow a device by its code Maintenance · Titles to fix, automatic subtitles, missing episodes, movie collections, seek bar previews, and on the Jellyfin PC: backup and update of Jellyfin, conversions with the graphics card The guide (? in the rail, F1 on Windows) is separate: where your videos go, and the Mira on your iPhone card that gets the server ready.

The Settings tab has: Account: your server, your account, your photo, Sign out. Playback: languages, intros and recaps, next episode, resume a little earlier. Away from home: Built-in Tailscale and the path Mira takes to Jellyfin. Administration (Jellyfin administrator): who is watching on Jellyfin right now. This iPhone → Privacy: everything Mira sends, to whom and when, and Built-in Tailscale's switch. About: the version and the source code.

Mira speaks English and French. By default it follows the language you chose when installing it, otherwise your system's. Change it in Settings → Appearance → Mira's language: it applies the next time Mira opens. The default audio and subtitle languages follow it.

For a PC or a Mac plugged into the TV, watched from the couch (Windows and Mac). Turn it on in Settings → Appearance → Couch mode: it applies at once, and stays on the next times Mira opens. Mira fills the whole screen, and every page is drawn larger, as on a 1280 × 720 window: readable from across the room. The player keeps its size. A white ring shows what is selected. The arrow keys go from one thing to the next anywhere on the screen, the rail included; Enter opens, Esc or Backspace goes back. In the player, Esc or Backspace stops the film and goes back to its page, as on a TV. A game controller (Xbox, or one that works as one; PlayStation and other controllers paired with a Mac): A opens, B goes back, Y searches, LB and RB change page. In the player, A pauses, X turns subtitles on or off, Y skips the intro, LB and RB jump a minute. Plug a controller in with couch mode off and Mira offers to turn it on. A TV remote, through the TV's HDMI-CEC with an adapter that types keys: its arrows, OK and back work like the keyboard's, and its play and pause keys reach Mira like a keyboard's media keys. Note Couch mode reads the controller only while Mira is in front, and sends nothing anywhere. To leave it, Settings → Appearance → Couch mode again.

What Mira sends, to whom and when. No account, no analytics, no telemetry. Mira has no account, no ads, no analytics and no telemetry. It talks to your Jellyfin server, and to a few services only when a feature needs them, each listed below. The code is open: see for yourself. Tip The same list is in the apps: Settings → Privacy on Windows, Mac and iPhone, each connection with what it sends and its switch, where it has one (the update check, Built-in Tailscale, and on Windows the check for a newer Jellyfin).

Who · To · What Mira, every device · your Jellyfin server · your library, playback and progress, with your session's token in a header, never in an address (except the iPhone's player stream, which Apple's player cannot send otherwise) Mira for Windows and Mac · GitHub (api.github.com) · the update check, at startup then every 6 hours: the request itself (your IP address, Mira's version), nothing else. Turn it off in Settings → Mira on this PC → Update automatically Before you sign in, Mira looks for Jellyfin on this computer, on your home network (Jellyfin's discovery question, never beyond your network) and on your Tailscale devices. Nothing identifying is sent; your password goes only to the address you sign in to.

s: Only when you use a feature
t: Feature · Contacts · What Built-in Tailscale, once you sign in to it · Tailscale's coordination servers and relays · like the Tailscale app: the account you chose, the device's name, its system and IP addresses, its public key. Videos stay end-to-end encrypted. No logs sent The mpv engine (Windows) · SourceForge · the download of the engine, SHA-256 checked Installing or updating Jellyfin (Windows) · repo.jellyfin.org, GitHub (winget's catalogue, once a day on the Jellyfin PC, off in Settings → Privacy) · the download, and whether a newer version exists Automatic subtitles · OpenSubtitles, SubDL, from your server · the file's fingerprint and size, IMDb/TMDb ids, season, episode, title, year, language. Never the file's name Search for subtitles… with another Jellyfin plugin · that plugin's service, from your server · what the plugin sends; Mira tells you before Your party link through Tailscale Funnel · Tailscale's relays, then your guests · your guests' traffic to Mira's page, encrypted to your PC. Your PC's Tailscale name becomes public A trailer from the web, at your click · the trailer's site (often YouTube), in your browser · what your browser sends (your IP address, the site's cookies). Mira loads nothing from it before your click and has no web view; a trailer kept on your server goes through it alone AltStore (iPhone) · Apple, miracinema.app, GitHub · your Apple ID to Apple only, for the free certificate; Mira's source and app

Your Jellyfin password is never stored: only the session. Windows protects it for your account; Mac and iPhone keep it in the keychain (on iPhone, this device only, never in backups). Built-in Tailscale's keys and state are encrypted on the device. Its log stays there and holds no sign-in page. Nothing about you or your library is ever collected. Full details, for each request: SECURITY.md (in French).
Found a security issue? Use Security → Report a vulnerability on Mira's GitHub repository, never a public issue. Never post a token, a session file or a password anywhere public.

The messages Mira shows when something is wrong, what they mean and what to do. Mira says what is wrong in its own words, with a button that helps when there is one. Find the message below, or search this wiki for a word of it.

Message or symptom · What to do Works at home, not away · The home address (192.168…) only works on your Wi-Fi. Use Tailscale: on the Jellyfin PC, the guide's Set everything up; on your device, Built-in Tailscale or the Tailscale app. "… isn't connected to Tailscale: it's off, asleep or offline" · The Jellyfin PC left Tailscale. Turn it on or wake it. Mira reloads Home as soon as it is back. Unreachable after a while without using the Jellyfin PC · It went to sleep, and Tailscale cannot wake it. Set everything up keeps it awake on mains power; on a laptop, set closing the lid to Do nothing on mains power. Unreachable after the Jellyfin PC restarted, until someone signs in to Windows · Tailscale waits for a session: Set everything up turns on Run unattended, or Tailscale's menu → Preferences → Run unattended. Tailscale asks to sign in again on the Jellyfin PC · Its key expired (every 180 days by default). Sign in again, then in the admin console, ⋯ → Disable key expiry on that PC. "Waiting for approval in Tailscale's admin console" · Your Tailscale network approves each new device: Open Tailscale's admin console and approve the device. Everything shows "Connecting…", on every device · Tailscale itself may be down: check status.tailscale.com. See When Tailscale itself is down. "Windows Security blocks mira-tailscale.exe" · An antivirus blocks Built-in Tailscale. Install the Tailscale app on this PC instead: Mira then goes through it. "macOS blocks mira-tailscale" · The "downloaded from the Internet" mark stayed on Mira.app: Copy the command in Built-in Tailscale's settings, paste it in Terminal, restart Mira. The iPhone doesn't see Jellyfin at home · iOS's local network access is off: Settings → Apps → Mira → Local Network. "Jellyfin is stopped on this PC" · Start Jellyfin, in the notice or on the guide's card. If it stops again, Mira shows the cause from Jellyfin's log (port 8096 taken, disk full…).

Message · What to do "This isn't a Jellyfin server" · Something else answers at that address (router, NAS, Emby): check the port, 8096 by default. "Mira needs Jellyfin 10.9" · Update Jellyfin. "HTTPS certificate not recognised" · For a server at home, type its full http:// address (Mira suggests it). Otherwise, install a valid certificate. "This address goes over the Internet, in http://" · Your password would travel unencrypted. Use the https:// or Tailscale address. "This Jellyfin already has an administrator account" · Its setup was started with another account: finish it on http://127.0.0.1:8096, then sign in. "Another program already answers on port 8096" · It isn't Jellyfin: close that program, or install Jellyfin on another PC.

Symptom · What to do Library shows, nothing plays (Windows) · Settings → Playback: install the mpv engine, or pick a 64-bit libmpv DLL. "The video engine couldn't be downloaded" · Check the Internet connection, then try again from Settings → Playback. It comes from downloads.sourceforge.net. Stutters away from home · Lower Quality in the player's ⋮ menu, or choose Auto. Picture stutters or stays black (Windows) · Turn off Hardware decoding in Settings → Playback. Grey or black picture (Mac) · In the player, ⋮ → Grey or black picture? Repair. Each repair goes one step further; Mira keeps the one that works. "Can't play this" · Mira reopened the stream and Jellyfin still could not serve the file. Jellyfin's administrator finds the reason in Settings → Maintenance → Reported playback failures. A file was added but doesn't show · Check it is in Movies, Shows or Anime, and named the way Jellyfin expects (see Name your videos). Then Refresh in the library.

Symptom · What to do Windows: an update doesn't install · Settings → Mira on this PC shows the last error; data\updates\update.log has the details. Mira's folder must stay writable. Mac: Mira asks for the keychain after an update · Only after an update made by Homebrew or by hand, once per version: choose Always Allow. See Install on Mac. iPhone: Mira no longer opens · It expired after 7 days. Open AltStore at home and tap Refresh All. Nothing is lost.

Ask on Discord, or open an issue with the versions of Mira, your system and Jellyfin. Never attach a password, a token, Mira's data folder or personal media. On Mac, a player log helps: in Terminal, MIRA_MPV_LOG=$HOME/Desktop/mpv.log /Applications/Mira.app/Contents/MacOS/Mira writes mpv.log on your desktop.
Short answers to what people ask most about Mira. Is Mira free? Yes, entirely, with no account, subscription or ads. Its code is open, under the MIT licence.
No. Mira plays what is on your own Jellyfin server. It provides no films, no sources and no content.
Yes: Jellyfin is the server that keeps your videos and serves them. If you don't have it, Mira for Windows installs it on your PC and sets it up for you. See Set up Jellyfin.

s: Can I use Mira with Plex or Emby?
t: No, only Jellyfin (10.9 or later).

s: Is there Mira for Android, a TV or a browser?
t: Not for now. Mira web, which played in the phone's browser, ended with 0.9.4 to focus on the apps. On a TV or a console, Jellyfin's own app works with the same server: Mira's guide gives the address to type.

s: Why isn't Mira on the App Store?
t: Publishing there needs a paid Apple developer account. AltStore Classic installs Mira with a free Apple ID instead: see Install on iPhone.

s: Why does Windows or macOS warn me?
t: Mira's files are not signed by a paid certificate yet. Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper warn about any unsigned app. Each file's SHA-256 is published next to it, in a release that can no longer be changed. See Install on Windows and Install on Mac.
At home, no: Mira plays every file as it is, 4K and HDR included. Away from home, if you set a lower Quality, Jellyfin converts the file while you watch.

s: Can my friends watch my library?
t: Two ways. Give them an account of their own (Settings → Friends & guests → Add a friend, as Jellyfin's administrator): they choose what to watch, when they want, and need Tailscale to reach your server from their home. Or send your party link: they watch with you, in your group, with no account and no Tailscale.

s: Is it safe to open my server to friends?
t: Your party link only opens Mira's page and its guest gateway to the Internet, never Jellyfin's dashboard or sign-in. Each guest has a limited hidden account that you can take back at any time. Accounts you create for friends can only see the libraries you chose, without downloads.
Your library, progress and accounts are on your Jellyfin server. Mira keeps a cache and your settings on each device, and nothing anywhere else. See Privacy.
Tell others, report bugs on GitHub, share ideas on Discord. Each page of this wiki has Edit this page on GitHub at the bottom.
